work: Design and Security Validation of Image-Agnostic Visual Semantic Authentication (VSA) Framework Based on Vision-Language Model
year_venue_status: 2026; Journal of The Korea Institute of Information Security and Cryptology 36(3), 935-948; peer-reviewed/KCI; DOI 10.13089/JKIISC.2026.36.3.935
representation: Grounding DINO + CLIP; objects, attributes, quantities, 2x2 quadrant spatial information; explicit semantic policies
matching: FlexibleRange Logic; 16 policies across five complexity levels
privacy_mechanism: Hash-based secret binding described as server-opaque in the verified abstract
threat_model_or_attacks: Image disclosure and shoulder surfing are explicit motivations; COCO-based FAR/FRR evaluation. Detailed database/key compromise, inversion, linkability, and attacker-oracle model were not established by the accessible authoritative abstract
offline_attack_property: Not established by the accessible authoritative abstract; hash binding alone must not be treated as proof against candidate validation after compromise
main_limitation_relative_to_project: Verified abstract does not report private computation of approximate matching, acceptance-region probability under semantic guess distributions, generative re-creation, or the project's A2-A7 evaluation. Full paper must be retrieved/translated before reproducing its policy baseline
relation_to_project: Closest work and mandatory baseline. It defeats any first-semantic/image-agnostic-authentication claim; the provisional gap is private approximate matching plus compromise/linkability/guessing analysis and independent generation
verification_note: Bibliography/abstract cross-checked against KCI and Korea's official national knowledge portal on 2026-08-24; unresolved full-text fields are marked rather than inferred

work: PassPoints: Design and Longitudinal Evaluation of a Graphical Password System
year_venue_status: 2005; International Journal of Human-Computer Studies 63(1-2), 102-127; peer-reviewed; DOI 10.1016/j.ijhcs.2005.04.010
representation: Ordered click points on a specific image
privacy_mechanism: None beyond conventional password storage/binding in the studied concept
threat_model_or_attacks: Usability, tolerance and longitudinal recall; not a privacy-template study
main_limitation_relative_to_project: Image-specific and human-study based; does not protect noisy semantic templates
relation_to_project: Historical graphical-password comparator and warning that tolerance/security/usability are distinct; its human results cannot support this no-human-study project

work: The Quest to Replace Passwords: A Framework for Comparative Evaluation of Web Authentication Schemes
year_venue_status: 2012; IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy, 553-567; peer-reviewed; DOI 10.1109/SP.2012.44
problem: Compare password-replacement schemes across usability, deployability and security
main_limitation_relative_to_project: Does not study semantic credentials or private fuzzy matching
relation_to_project: Sanity-check framework: do not call the proposal a password replacement without deployment/security evidence; second-factor positioning remains valid
verification_note: Primary conference PDF and DOI metadata verified 2026-08-24

work: Fuzzy Extractors: How to Generate Strong Keys from Biometrics and Other Noisy Data
year_venue_status: 2008; SIAM Journal on Computing 38(1), 97-139; peer-reviewed; preliminary EUROCRYPT 2004 version
problem: Generate stable strong keys from noisy nonuniform sources
representation: Metric-space noisy source plus public helper data/secure sketch
matching: Recovery within Hamming, edit, set-difference and other supported distances
threat_model_or_attacks: Helper-data leakage and source min-entropy are central formal parameters
offline_attack_property: Security depends on residual source entropy after public helper data; low/nonuniform semantic distributions require explicit analysis
main_limitation_relative_to_project: Does not establish that user-chosen semantic sources have sufficient min-entropy or that their acceptance regions map cleanly to a chosen metric
relation_to_project: Primary theoretical basis for fuzzy-recovery candidate and its elimination criteria
verification_note: Author-maintained page and journal-version metadata verified 2026-08-24

work: Neural Fuzzy Extractors: A Secure Way to Use Artificial Neural Networks for Biometric User Authentication
year_venue_status: 2022; Proceedings on Privacy Enhancing Technologies 2022(4), 86-104; peer-reviewed; DOI 10.56553/popets-2022-0100
representation: Classifier output transformed by neural expander into fuzzy-extractor-compatible space
privacy_mechanism: Neural expander + secure sketch/fuzzy extractor + hash comparison
threat_model_or_attacks: Stolen classifier/template structures and synthetic inputs; simple biometric scenarios
offline_attack_property: Inherits fuzzy-extractor entropy/helper assumptions; application to low-entropy semantic concepts is not demonstrated
approximate_matching: Yes, learned clusters plus fuzzy recovery
main_limitation_relative_to_project: Biometric class setting; does not establish security/correctness for user-chosen semantic sets or AI-assisted semantic dictionaries
relation_to_project: Strong PoPETs baseline for the fuzzy-extractor branch and evidence that learned recovery is prior art

work: Oblivious Pseudorandom Functions (OPRFs) Using Prime-Order Groups
problem: Standardised OPRF, VOPRF and POPRF evaluations
representation: Opaque byte-string input to keyed PRF
matching: Exact function evaluation, optionally verifiable/partially oblivious
threat_model_or_attacks: Server should not learn client input/output; client should not learn server key; security assumptions and domain separation specified
offline_attack_property: The primitive alone does not define stored records, threshold set matching, rate limits, or protection once the relevant server key and records are compromised
main_limitation_relative_to_project: Does not by itself provide PSI, threshold matching, authentication, or full-compromise resistance
relation_to_project: Mature primitive candidate; project novelty cannot be OPRF alone and must analyse key/service compromise

work: The OPAQUE Augmented Password-Authenticated Key Exchange (aPAKE) Protocol
problem: Password-hidden mutual authentication and key exchange
representation: Exact password-derived OPRF output and encrypted credential envelope
threat_model_or_attacks: Server mishandling, precomputation after compromise, online guessing, forward secrecy and KCI considerations
offline_attack_property: RFC explicitly states offline dictionary attack after server credential-file compromise is inevitable, while OPAQUE resists precomputation and hides the password from the server/registration
main_limitation_relative_to_project: Does not solve fuzzy recovery or low semantic entropy; must be composed with and analysed alongside a noisy-source construction
relation_to_project: Mature PAKE for fuzzy-recovery candidate; prevents overclaim that OPAQUE automatically solves noisy semantics/offline guessing

work: Phasing: Private Set Intersection Using Permutation-based Hashing
problem: Efficient private set intersection at practical scales
representation: Private sets encoded with permutation-based hashing
threat_model_or_attacks: Two parties should learn no more than the intersection under the protocol model
offline_attack_property: Does not define persistent authentication records or semantic-dictionary resistance after server/key compromise
approximate_matching: Exact intersection only; a separate cardinality/threshold construction is needed
main_limitation_relative_to_project: Reveals the intersection rather than only Accept/Reject and does not address noisy semantic authentication
relation_to_project: Primary PSI performance/design anchor; shows PSI is mature prior art while threshold-only leakage and compromise handling remain project work

work: HyDia: FHE-based Facial Matching with Hybrid Approximations and Diagonalization
year_venue_status: 2025; Proceedings on Privacy Enhancing Technologies 2025(4), 585-604; peer-reviewed; DOI 10.56553/popets-2025-0146
representation: Dense facial feature vectors encrypted under CKKS FHE
matching: Homomorphic inner product and approximate thresholding
privacy_mechanism: Fully homomorphic encryption with hybrid polynomial approximation
threat_model_or_attacks: Protect plaintext biometric/query and avoid revealing exact similarity scores; formal proof and compromise details are construction-specific
offline_attack_property: Encrypted records prevent plaintext access under the stated key model; project must separately evaluate client/decryption-key compromise and semantic guessability
approximate_matching: Yes, encrypted vector similarity with threshold-only result
main_limitation_relative_to_project: Biometric identification with dense vectors, not low-entropy user-chosen semantic secrets; FHE protects computation but not acceptance-region guessability
relation_to_project: Closest PoPETs encrypted-vector/private-threshold baseline and evidence that private threshold similarity is established prior art
verification_note: Official PoPETs record and artifact status verified 2026-08-24

problem: Measure sensitive information leaked by embeddings
matching: Attack classifiers, inversion and membership inference
threat_model_or_attacks: Embedding inversion, attribute inference and membership inference
offline_attack_property: Stored embeddings can expose recoverable input/attribute information without an offline password verifier
main_limitation_relative_to_project: Experiments focus on text embeddings, not the selected vision/semantic models
relation_to_project: Mandatory warning and attack-method anchor: raw dense embeddings are not private credentials
verification_note: ACM proceedings/DBLP DOI and metadata verified 2026-08-24

work: Unlinkable and Irreversible Biometric Template Protection Based on Bloom Filters
problem: Evaluate and construct unlinkable/irreversible protected biometric templates
representation: Bloom-filter transformed face templates with secret-conditioned rearrangement
threat_model_or_attacks: Protected-template and full-disclosure attackers; reconstruction and cross-matching
offline_attack_property: Shows that apparently protected deterministic templates can admit brute-force cross-matching; evaluates stronger transformed records
main_limitation_relative_to_project: Biometric template scheme, not semantic-set authentication; does not resolve semantic dictionaries
relation_to_project: Methodological anchor for A6/A7 metrics and warning that unlinkability must be attacked, not assumed from salting/hashing

problem: Requirements for confidentiality, integrity, renewability/revocability and privacy-compliant biometric processing
representation: Biometric references and identity references across storage/comparison architectures
privacy_mechanism: Requirements and guidance, not one mechanism
threat_model_or_attacks: Threat/countermeasure analysis, secure binding, storage/comparison models and privacy
main_limitation_relative_to_project: Biometric-specific and paywalled in full; not a semantic-authentication protocol
relation_to_project: Requirements anchor for irreversibility, unlinkability, renewability and performance-preservation concepts used in A6/A7

work: DiffusionDB: A Large-scale Prompt Gallery Dataset for Text-to-Image Generative Models
problem: Study real text-to-image prompts and model interaction
representation: 14 million Stable Diffusion images, 1.8 million unique user-specified prompts and hyperparameters
privacy_mechanism: CC0 dataset; no authentication privacy mechanism
threat_model_or_attacks: Dataset harms/content and prompt-distribution analysis; not an authentication threat model
main_limitation_relative_to_project: Prompts are image-generation requests, not authentication-secret choices; contributor/privacy/content limitations require filtering
relation_to_project: Candidate empirical dictionary/frequency source for A4 only; cannot support claims about natural credential selection

work: PassGPT: Password Modeling and (Guided) Generation with Large Language Models
problem: Model and generate password guesses, including constrained generation
representation: Transformer language model trained on leaked passwords
threat_model_or_attacks: Offline password guessing with generative models
offline_attack_property: Improves candidate ordering but does not change verifier properties
main_limitation_relative_to_project: Password leaks and exact strings differ from semantic concepts/acceptance regions
relation_to_project: Evidence that generative guessing is established; motivates but does not substitute for a semantic-specific A4 attack methodology
